newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst says it reduced its debt in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst says it reduced its debt in 1996.

text.p: German chemicals and drugs group Hoechst AG said on Wednedsay that its corporate debt had fallen by some 900 million marks last year.
The group's corporate debt totalled 11.8 billion marks last year compared with 12.730 billion marks in 1995.

In the annual report Hoechst said that 2.4 billion marks in liquid funds generated by divestments had been used to reduce the debt. On the other hand the acquisition of Plant Genetic Systems by Hoechst's AgrEvo unit had increased the debt level by 700 million marks. Exchange rate movements increased the debt by 700 million marks compared with 1995, Hoechst said.
The long-term corporate debt is currently being financed at an average interest rate of 6.5 percent, the group said.
